sources.entry: homebrew-cask - A CLI workflow for the administration of macOS applications distributed as binaries

summary.one_liner: Homebrew Cask is a command-line workflow for installing and managing prebuilt macOS and Linux software artifacts, such as GUI apps, CLI tools, and fonts, distributed by upstream vendors.
summary.what_it_does: Extends Homebrew so that prebuilt software artifacts from upstream vendors can be installed and managed from the terminal. The README covers GUI applications, CLI tools, fonts, and plugins. The example shows `brew install alfred` downloading, verifying, and moving the app into /Applications with no manual dragging. The README points to USAGE.md for basic usage and CONTRIBUTING.md for adding a new cask. It also describes a reporting process that asks users to run `brew update-reset && brew update` before filing bugs and links to guides for common errors such as curl, permission, and checksum failures. Issues requesting new casks are closed; new casks go in through pull requests.
use_cases: install macOS apps from the terminal
script app installation on a new Mac
manage GUI applications with a package manager
install fonts or plugins via command line
how_to_run: Install Homebrew first (the README says only Homebrew is needed)
notable: Installs GUI apps by name with one command, e.g. `brew install alfred`
Covers GUI apps, CLI tools, fonts, and plugins distributed as prebuilt artifacts
Documentation split across USAGE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md
Includes a guide to common errors such as checksum mismatches and permission problems
caveats: Requires Homebrew to already be installed
Issues requesting new casks are closed without review; new casks must be submitted as pull requests
The README asks users to try a reset-and-update step before reporting bugs, and issues may be closed without review if the guide is ignored
